{{Quote|They're the most beautiful creatures in the universe. They live on the moons of Iego, I think.|Anakin Skywalker, describing the "Angels" of Iego|<ref name="Phantom">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
The '''Diathim''', also referred to as '''Angels''', were a mysterious [[Species/Legends|species]] of winged [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] who inhabited the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Iego/Legends|Iego]] and [[Millius Prime/Legends|Millius Prime]], the largest of its [[Moons of Iego/Legends|many]] [[Moon/Legends|moons]]. The Diathim were reputed for their beauty, and the way in which they appeared would vary depending on the beholder. They shared their habitat with the [[Maelibus|Maelibi]], who lived below the ground. When the young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] first met his future wife [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], he compared her natural beauty to that of the Diathim.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|They are good and kind, and so pretty they make even the most hardened space pirates cry like small children.|Anakin Skywalker on the "Angels"|<ref name="Phantom_novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Diathim.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Diathim in flight]]
The mysterious [[Species/Legends|species]] whom the [[University of Sanbra]] [[Xenobiology|xenobiologists]] called "the Diathim," otherwise known as "the Angels," seemed to be made of blazing [[Color/Legends|white]] light tinged with a yellow aura,<ref name="GORW" /> which suggested they were beings of pure energy.<ref name="FF30 2014" /> At any rate, their intense radiance made it difficult to make out their biological details. Most accounts depicted them as slender, 2 to 3 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall [[Gender/Legends|feminine]] [[Humanoid/Legends|anthropoids]] with six blade-shaped wings protruding from their backs.<ref name="GORW" /> One particular [[Diathim refugee/Legends|individual]] appeared in front of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], two [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], as a tall woman of their species with wings, [[Milk/Legends|milky]] white skin, blond [[Hair/Legends|hair]], light blue [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a tiny [[Nose/Legends|nose]] and long [[Limb/Legends|limbs]].<ref name="Moon" /> Some other witnesses described the Angels as more androgynous, while many [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]] observers portrayed them as mysterious and fascinating variants of their own species. Whether their wings were physical or not, the Diathim could fly and glide freely.<ref name="GORW" /> They could even fly in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of interplanetary [[Realspace/Legends|space]] without the assistance of a protective suit or life support. They also had natural [[Hypnosis|hypnotic]] abilities.<ref name="FF30 2014" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|They were also supposed to be good and kind&mdash;two words you don't hear much on Tatooine.|Anakin Skywalker on the "Angels"|<ref name="EP1J/AS">''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref>}}
The Diathim gave off an aura of kindness,<ref name="GORW" /> and they were consistently described as benevolent by those spacers who propagated the legend of the Angels.<ref name="EP1J/AS" /> They described themselves as a peaceful people.<ref name="Moon" /> However, the Diathim were fascinated by [[Starship/Legends|spacecrafts]], which often prompted them to mob any ships that found themselves in the vicinity of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]], [[Iego/Legends|Iego]] and [[Millius Prime/Legends|Millius Prime]].<ref name="FF30 2014" /> Because of their hypnotic abilities, those curious Diathim had a tendency to provoke accidents, causing the mesmerized observers to plunge their vessels into violent crash-landings.<ref name="GORW" /> For those reasons, they were still regarded as dangerous entities.<ref name="FF30 2014" />

Since the Diathim were only seen when they gathered in flocks to welcome arriving ships, knowledge of what their habitat looked like remained hidden to outsiders. Although they had no apparent [[Language/Legends|language]] of their own,<ref name="GORW" /> at least some of them were capable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]],<ref name="Moon" /> the common language of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="SW RPG">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|We were a peaceful people before the Separatists drove us from our homes and stole our moon.|A Diathim refugee, to Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Moon" />}}
[[File:Angel1.png|thumb|250px|A Diathim refugee during the Clone Wars]]
The Diathim evolved in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of Iego and the largest of its [[Moons of Iego/Legends|forty-two moons]], Millius Prime. They shared those worlds with the [[Maelibus|Maelibi]], a species of three-meter tall burrowing beings who [[Diet/Legends|fed]] on castaways.<ref name="FF30 2014" /> They were known in the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] as early as [[25,793 BBY]],<ref name="Void">''[[Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void]]''</ref> more than seven [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] before the founding of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TORE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> At the time, the Basic idiom "space angel" referred to a selfless, innocent person.<ref name="Void" />

Millennia later, during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], some Diathim were driven from their home on Millius Prime when a [[LaserWeb Defense Station/Legends|laser grid system]] was installed there by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] to keep people from leaving. The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker travelled to Iego with his [[Jedi Master/Legends|master]] Obi-Wan Kenobi while on a [[Mission to Iego/Legends|mission]] to uncover a [[Reeksa/Legends|root]] said to contain the antidote to the [[Blue Shadow Virus/Legends|Blue Shadow Virus]]. The two encountered one of the Diathim refugees, and the Jedi eventually managed to deactivate the laser field, thus freeing the inhabitants of Iego.<ref name="Moon" />

==Angels in the galaxy==
[[File:Anakin_Meets_Padme.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Anakin Skywalker mistook Padmé Amidala for a Diathim.]]
{{Quote|I looked closer and instantly knew that she was the most beautiful creature I had ever seen. In fact, I was certain that I was in the presence of an angel, even though I'd never met one before.|Anakin Skywalker, on his first encounter with Padmé Amidala|<ref name="EP1J/AS" />}}
When a young Anakin Skywalker lived on the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], he first heard of the Diathim's proverbial beauty while listening to all the [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] and [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] who stopped there. Those tales influenced Skywalker's first words to his future [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], questioning whether or not she was indeed one of those legendary beings. The boy believed Amidala's beauty unmatched, and seemed to think this led to some connections with the famed Diathim of Iego.<ref name="Phantom" /> When Amidala answered that she had never heard of Angels before, Skywalker objected she just might be unaware of her true nature.<ref name="Phantom_novel" />

==Behind the scenes==
Angels were first mentioned by Anakin Skywalker in the [[1999]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the first installment of the [[prequel trilogy]] of ''[[Star Wars]]''. Skywalker's line "Are you an Angel?" ({{Audio|Angel-TPM.flac|Listen}})<ref name="Phantom" /> was later spoofed in the [[2004]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' as an [[Easter egg (virtual)|easter egg]]. In a conversation that only appears after the player has completed the game at least once as a lightsider and once as a darksider, [[Atton Rand]] repeats Skywalker's line from ''The Phantom Menace'' upon seeing [[Meetra Surik]] for the first time, in her undergarments. Rand then promptly recants, stating that it was "the worst line [he's] ever used" and hoping that "some poor kid doesn't start using it."<ref name="kotor-2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

In [[Wikipedia:Abrahamic religions|Abrahamic religions]], angels are spiritual beings that act as messengers from [[Wikipedia:God in Abrahamic religions|God]] and as guardians of human beings. In art, they are often depicted as glowing humans dressed in flowing robes with bird-like wings.<ref name="birdo">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-imagination-mythological-creatures-in-star-wars-part-2|text=Drawing from the Imagination: Mythological Creatures in ''Star Wars'', Part 2|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref>

An Angels later first appeared in "[[Mystery of a Thousand Moons]]," the eighteenth episode of [[The Clone Wars: Season One|Season One]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, where they are voiced by actress [[Catherine Taber]], who coincidentally voiced Padmé Amidala in the same series.<ref name="Moon-EG">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode018.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Mystery of a Thousand Moons}}</ref>  The characters went through multiple revisions with some being less human.<ref name="Mystery EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/mystery-of-a-thousand-moons-episode-guide|text="Mystery of a Thousand Moons" Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars}}</ref> Early concept art of the character close to the final design was done by [[Jackson Sze]].<ref name="Art of TCW">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''</ref>
